text:
And this point, too, is hard to see, namely the stilling
   of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction
   of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.

say: And this point, too, is hard to see, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.

Just as a woman or a man, youthful and fond of adornment, in looking
at her or his facial image in a mirror or in a bowl filled with pure,
clear, clean water, would be seeing it with dependence and not without
dependence.

say: Just as a woman or a man, youthful and fond of adornment, in looking at her or his facial image in a mirror or in a bowl filled with pure, clear, clean water, would be seeing it with dependence and not without dependence.

text:
The world arises in the six sense-bases. It is at the same time the
arising of suffering... The law of dependent arising is an explanation
of the way a concept of the world comes about. This is an extremely
subtle point.

say: The world arises in the six sense-bases. It is at the same time the arising of suffering... The law of dependent arising is an explanation of the way a concept of the world comes about. This is an extremely subtle point.

text:
The deepest point of the entire formula of paticca samuppada is
traceable to the interrelation that obtains between name and form on
the one hand, and between name-and-form and consciousness on the other.

say: The deepest point of the entire formula of paticca samuppada is traceable to the interrelation that obtains between name and form on the one hand, and between name-and-form and consciousness on the other.

text:
Like an expert physician, who treats the germ of a disease and
immunizes the patient, the Buddha effected a breach in the saṃsāric
vortex by concentrating on its epicycle within this fathom-long body.

say: Like an expert physician, who treats the germ of a disease and immunizes the patient, the Buddha effected a breach in the samsaric vortex by concentrating on its epicycle within this fathom-long body.

text:
All the twelve links are dependently arisen, and avijjā is no
exception. Even ignorance arises with the arising of influxes,
āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayo. So even ignorance is not the cause. The
cause is the underlying principle itself.

say: All the twelve links are dependently arisen, and avijja is no exception. Even not seeing how it works arises with the arising of influxes, asavasamudaya avijjasamudayo. So even not seeing how it works is not the cause. The cause is the underlying principle itself.

text:
What is called the cessation of consciousness has a deeper sense here.
It means the cessation of the specifically prepared consciousness,
abhisaikhata vinnana. An arahant's experience of the cessation of
consciousness is at the same time the experience of the cessation of
name-and-form.

say: What is called the stopping of consciousness has a deeper sense here. It means the stopping of the specifically prepared consciousness, abhisaikhata vinnana — just knowing, before words. An arahant's experience of the stopping of consciousness is at the same time the experience of the stopping of name-and-form.

text:
True to the qualities of the Dhamma — to be seen here and now, not
involving time, and inviting to come and see — the entire mass of samsaric
suffering ceases immediately.

say: True to the qualities of the Dhamma — to be seen here and now, not involving time, and inviting to come and see — the entire mass of samsaric suffering ceases immediately.

text:
In order to ascertain whether a banana trunk is pith-less, it is not
necessary to go on removing its bark, layer after layer, from top to
bottom. We only have to take a sharp sword and cut the trunk in the
middle, so that the cross-section will reveal to us its pith-less nature.
Similarly, if we cut in the middle the banana trunk of preparations with
the sharp sword of wisdom, its internal structure as revealed by the
cross-section will convince us of the essence-less nature of the group
of preparations.

say: In order to ascertain whether a banana trunk is pith-less, it is not necessary to go on removing its bark, layer after layer, from top to bottom. We only have to take a sharp sword and cut the trunk in the middle, so that the cross-section will reveal to us its pith-less nature. Similarly, if we cut in the middle the banana trunk of things the mind makes with the sharp sword of wisdom, its internal structure as revealed by the cross-section will convince us of the essence-less nature of the group of things the mind makes.

text:
According to the accepted interpretation, presented by the venerable
author of the Visuddhimagga, the first two links of the formula belong to
the past, and the last two links belong to the future. The remaining
eight links in the middle are taken to represent the present. That means,
we have here the three periods of time. So it is not — timeless.

say: According to the accepted interpretation, presented by the venerable author of the Visuddhimagga, the first two links of the formula belong to the past, and the last two links belong to the future. The remaining eight links in the middle are taken to represent the present. That means, we have here the three periods of time. So it is not — timeless.

text:
Sometimes we happen to buy from a shop an extremely rickety machine
deceived by its paint and polish, and take it home as a brand new
thing. The very next day it goes out of order... So is our birth with
its unpredictable vicissitudes... This is the price we pay for this
brand new body we are blessed with in this existence.

say: Sometimes we happen to buy from a shop an extremely rickety machine deceived by its paint and polish, and take it home as a brand new thing. The very next day it goes out of order... So is our birth with its unpredictable vicissitudes... This is the price we pay for this brand new body we are blessed with in this existence.

text:
In such discourses as the Bahudhātukasutta the twelve-linked formula
is introduced with a set of these thematic phrases, which is then
related to the formula proper with the conjunctive 'that is to say',
yadidaṃ. This conjunctive clearly indicates that the twelve-linked
formula is an illustration. The twelve links are therefore things
dependently arisen, paṭicca samuppannā dhammā.

say: In such discourses as the Bahudhatukasutta the twelve-linked formula is introduced with a set of these thematic phrases, which is then related to the formula proper with the conjunctive 'that is to say', yadidam. This conjunctive clearly indicates that the twelve-linked formula is an illustration. The twelve links are therefore things dependently arisen, paticca samuppanna dhamma.
